items.title: Gerald Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He writes arrangements – popular arrangements of Artie Shaw’s Frenesi. He wrote that arrangement for Artie Shaw.

ctx.x: And Zubin Mehta was the director at that time for the LA Philharmonic.
And that’s when – that’s when um, that’s when Zubin Mehta wanted to honor black composers. Black composers. So they had Ray Brown, the bass player – he’s going to be the

coordinator. He’s going to tell him the black composers that who – which should be there. Okay, and he had me on there, he had me on there. And he had – I’m not gonna call people’s name now, ‘cause I’m not naming any people here, but he – he lined up some guys that I would have said, too, you know. I would have said them, myself. So Oliver Nelson and I went to the University of Utah together, where we stayed for a week, where we both rehearsed with the band, played your music with your band at a concert. So I’d…
